title: Lifting a derived complex for a projective class
statement: Let $R$ be a ring, $I\subseteq R$ an ideal, $\mathcal P$ a class of $R$-modules, $K\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and $E^\bullet$ a complex of $R/I$-modules representing $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R/I$ in $D(R/I)$. Assume: (1) every member of $\mathcal P$ is projective; (2) $P_1\in\mathcal P$ and $P_1\oplus P_2\in\mathcal P$ if and only if $P_1,P_2\in\mathcal P$; (3) every map $f:P_1\to P_2$ with $P_1,P_2\in\mathcal P$ that is surjective modulo $I$ is surjective; (4) $E^\bullet$ is bounded above and each $E^i$ is isomorphic to $P/IP$ for some $P\in\mathcal P$; and (5) $K$ is represented by a bounded-above complex with terms in $\mathcal P$. Then $K$ is represented by a bounded-above complex $P^\bullet$ with terms in $\mathcal P$ whose termwise quotient $P^\bullet/IP^\bullet$ is isomorphic to $E^\bullet$ as a complex.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.75.2, proof and statement of lemma-lift-complex (general class of modules)

proof.text: By (5) choose a bounded-above complex $K^\bullet$ with terms in $\mathcal P$ representing $K$. Its terms are projective by (1), hence flat, so $K^\bullet$ is K-flat by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat]; therefore $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R/I$ is represented in $D(R/I)$ by the termwise quotient $K^\bullet/IK^\bullet=K^\bullet\otimes_R R/I$ by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] (one-point site, $\mathcal O=R$, $\mathcal O'=R/I$). Each $E^i\cong P/IP$ with $P$ projective is a projective $R/I$-module, so $E^\bullet$ is a bounded-above complex of projective $R/I$-modules; the isomorphism $E^\bullet\cong K^\bullet/IK^\bullet$ in $D(R/I)$ is therefore represented by a chain map $\delta:E^\bullet\to K^\bullet/IK^\bullet$ by [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative], and $\delta$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

Let $C^\bullet$ be the cone of $\delta$. Then $C^i=(K^i/IK^i)\oplus E^{i+1}$, which is of the form $P/IP$ with $P\in\mathcal P$ since $\mathcal P$ is closed under direct sums by (2); $C^\bullet$ is bounded above, and it is acyclic because $\delta$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The map $q:K^\bullet\to K^\bullet/IK^\bullet\to C^\bullet$ (reduction followed by the cone inclusion) is a chain map.

Apply [lem-sc-complex-lift-acyclic-projective] (its hypotheses are (1), the 'only if' half of (2), and (3)) to obtain a bounded-above acyclic complex $A^\bullet$ with terms in $\mathcal P$ and an isomorphism $A^\bullet/IA^\bullet\cong C^\bullet$; let $\pi:A^\bullet\to C^\bullet$ be the resulting termwise surjective chain map. As $A^\bullet$ and $C^\bullet$ are both acyclic, $\pi$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

We find a chain map $h:K^\bullet\to A^\bullet$ with $\pi\circ h=q$ exactly (the dotted arrow). Since $Q(\pi)$ is invertible in $D(R)$, the morphism $Q(\pi)^{-1}Q(q):K^\bullet\to A^\bullet$ is represented by a chain map $h_0$ by [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative] ($K^\bullet$ is a bounded-above complex of projectives). Then $Q(\pi h_0)=Q(q)$, so by the injectivity in the same statement (target $C^\bullet$) $\pi h_0-q=ds+sd$ for maps $s^i:K^i\to C^{i-1}$. As $K^i$ is projective and $\pi$ is termwise surjective, lift $s^i$ to $\tilde s^i:K^i\to A^{i-1}$, and put $h=h_0-(d\tilde s+\tilde sd)$; this is a chain map with $\pi h=q$. Thus the reduction of $h^i$ modulo $I$ is the cone inclusion $K^i/IK^i\to C^i=K^i/IK^i\oplus E^{i+1}$, a split injection whose cokernel $E^{i+1}$ is of the form $P/IP$ with $P\in\mathcal P$ by (4).

proof.text: Claim: if $f:P_1\to P_2$ with $P_1,P_2\in\mathcal P$ reduces modulo $I$ to a split injection with cokernel $P_3/IP_3$, $P_3\in\mathcal P$, then $f$ is split injective with cokernel isomorphic to $P_3$. Indeed, since $P_2$ is projective (1), lift the projection $P_2/IP_2\to P_3/IP_3$ to $g:P_2\to P_3$. By (3) $g$ is surjective, hence split by (1), so $P_2=P'_1\oplus P_3$ with $P'_1=\ker g\in\mathcal P$ by (2). The composite $P_1\to P_2\to P'_1$ is an isomorphism modulo $I$, hence surjective by (3) and split by (1): $P_1=T\oplus P'_1$ with $T\in\mathcal P$ by (2). Then $T/IT=0$; since $0\in\mathcal P$ (a summand of any member, by (2)), the map $0\to T$ is surjective modulo $I$, so $T=0$ by (3). Hence $P_1\to P'_1$ is an isomorphism, $f$ is split injective, and $\operatorname{coker} f\cong P_3$.

By the previous two steps each $h^i:K^i\to A^i$ is split injective with cokernel $Q^i\cong$ a member of $\mathcal P$, so $0\to K^\bullet\to A^\bullet\to Q^\bullet\to0$ is a termwise split short exact sequence of complexes with $Q^\bullet$ bounded above. Put $P^\bullet=Q^\bullet[-1]$, a bounded-above complex with terms in $\mathcal P$. Since $A^\bullet$ is acyclic, the associated distinguished triangle gives $K^\bullet\cong Q^\bullet[-1]=P^\bullet$ in $D(R)$, so $P^\bullet$ represents $K$. Reducing the termwise split sequence modulo $I$ stays exact, and by the previous step the reduction of $h$ is the cone inclusion $K^\bullet/IK^\bullet\to C^\bullet$, whose cokernel complex is $E^\bullet[1]$; hence $Q^\bullet/IQ^\bullet\cong E^\bullet[1]$ and $P^\bullet/IP^\bullet\cong E^\bullet$ as complexes.
